paper.title: Rethinking the Global Convergence of Softmax Policy Gradient with Linear Function Approximation: The Case of Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit with log-linear (Lin-SPG) policy, problem-specific learning rate
unmapped: policy is softmax of a fixed known feature matrix phi in R^{K x d} (d <= K) times parameter theta (log-linear policy class)
learner's step size depends on the min gap of the order-preserving projection Delta', and lambda_max(phi phi^T)
settings.definition_quote: We study the policy optimization problem for $K$-armed stochastic bandits ... $\mathbb{E}[R_t(a_t)\mid a_t=a,\mathcal{F}_t]=r(a)$ and $|R_t(a_t)|\le R_{\max}$ almost surely. ... $\pi_\theta = \softmax(\phi\,\theta)$

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit with log-linear (Lin-SPG) policy, arbitrary constant learning rate
unmapped: policy is softmax of a fixed known feature matrix phi in R^{K x d} (d <= K) times parameter theta (log-linear policy class)
settings.definition_quote: We study the policy optimization problem for $K$-armed stochastic bandits ... $|R_t(a_t)|\le R_{\max}$ almost surely. ... $\pi_\theta = \softmax(\phi\,\theta)$

algorithms.name: Lin-SPG (Softmax PG with linear function approximation, stochastic, on-policy IS estimates)

symbols.gamma_conv: gamma = (Delta*Delta')^2/(16 R_max^2), Delta' = min gap of the order-preserving projection phi w

conditions: Assumption 2: reward ordering preservation by some phi w
Assumption 4: feature conditions <phi_i - phi_j, phi_{a*} - phi_k> > 0 or >= 0
tuning: eta <= min{ sqrt(gamma)/(6 sqrt(2) lambda_max(phi phi^T)^{3/2} R_max), gamma^{3/2}/(6 rho lambda_max(phi phi^T)^{5/2}) }, rho = 8 R_max^3 K^{3/2}/Delta^2

source.label: theorem:softmax_pg_sublinear_rate
source.quote: Given a reward vector $r \in \mathbb{R}^{K}$ and a feature matrix $\phi \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times d}$ such that $d \leq K$ and Assumptions 1,2,4 are satisfied, Alg 2 with the constant learning rate $\eta$ as in (eq:step_size_for_stochastic_bandits) results in the following convergence rate that if $\mu \coloneq (\mathbb{E}[(\inf_{t\geq 1}\pi_{\theta_t}(a^\star))^{-2}])^{-1} > 0$, then ... $\leq\frac{2}{\eta\,\gamma\,\mu\,T}$.

results.notes: Quantity is expected suboptimality of the returned policy pi_{T+1}; mapped to simple_regret. Paper calls it a pseudo-rate since mu may be exponentially small. Rewards in [-R_max,R_max] mapped to bounded_pm1 with scale R_max. Step size requires Delta, R_max, K and feature-dependent quantities.

bound.expression_latex: \frac{\sum_{s=\tau}^T r(a^\star) - \dpd{\pis, r}}{T - \tau + 1} \leq \frac{2 R_{\max} \left[ \frac{K}{C} \ln \left( C\,T + e^C  \right) + \frac{\pi^2\,K}{6\,C} + K\,C^\prime \right] }{T - \tau + 1}
bound.regime: T > tau, for a sufficiently large (random) tau

symbols.C_tilde: random trajectory-dependent constant C > 0 from the theorem
symbols.tau: sufficiently large random iteration after which the bound holds

source.label: theorem:asymptotic_convergence_rate
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 1,4 hold. Using Alg 2 with any constant learning rate $\eta>0$, almost surely, there exist a sufficiently large $\tau\geq1$ and constants $C>0$ and $C'\geq0$ such that for all $T>\tau$, it holds that $\frac{\sum_{s=\tau}^T r(a^\star) - \dpd{\pis, r}}{T - \tau + 1} \leq \frac{2 R_{\max} [ \frac{K}{C} \ln ( C\,T + e^C ) + \frac{\pi^2\,K}{6\,C} + K\,C^\prime ] }{T - \tau + 1}$.

results.notes: Paper bounds the average suboptimality over rounds tau..T; multiplied by (T - tau + 1) to give cumulative policy-suboptimality sum_{s=tau}^T (r(a*) - <pi_s, r>). Constants C, C', tau are random and existential, so the bound is asymptotic O(log T) cumulative. Quantity labelled realized_regret since it is a random path-wise sum of expected per-round suboptimality.
